title: Kernel microhistogram & context envelope telemetry for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Maya Patel
description: Add a low-overhead, high-cardinality telemetry path that captures per-kernel microhistograms tied to an execution context envelope. Goal is to enable fast root-cause analysis of tail latency regressions in the prefill/decode scheduler and to provide cost-attribution signals for kernel choices without flooding tracing backends. The feature will: 1) emit compact, sketch-based microhistograms per kernel invocation cohort, keyed by an execution-context fingerprint (model, sequence bucket, schedule phase, routing decision); 2) publish a context envelope that aggregates NVTX span metadata, scheduler score, and placement hints so traces and histograms can be correlated offline; 3) expose aggregated views in Console (per-model, per-route, per-kernel) and add alerting for unexpected shifts in kernel latency distributions.
acceptance_criteria: Microhistogram protobuf and ingestion pipeline implemented and documented
End-to-end pipeline: runtime -> ingestion -> stores (TSDB for counts, object store for envelopes) -> Console visualizations
Overhead: additional CPU < 3% p99 and network overhead < 0.5 KB per request on median workload sampled at 1/100 requests
Correlation: given a trace ID, operator can locate the matching context envelope and microhistogram within 30s of ingestion
Rollout plan with sampling knobs, canary, and kill-switch in config
tasks: Design microhistogram schema (DDSketch-based) and context envelope protobuf
Instrument runtime to emit envelope + microhistogram at scheduler handoff points (prefill end, decode start/end)
Implement sampling policy: deterministic hash-based + dynamic downsampling for high-throughput customers
Build ingestion lambda and translate DDSketch to percentiles then store coalesced histograms
Console dashboards: per-model kernel latency heatmap, context join panel, timeline of scheduler decisions
End-to-end load test and cost analysis across representative workloads
Write runbook for triage and add an automated regression alert
notes: We prefer DDSketch for relative-error guarantees across heavy tails. Alternatives considered: HDR histogram (less space efficient for extreme tails) and t-digest (higher merge cost).
Context envelope keeps NVTX names but normalizes them to stable tokens to avoid high-cardinality free-text from model authors.
Privacy: envelopes will not include prompt text; only metadata hashes and non-identifying route/model ids.
Trade-off: higher sampling at canary yields faster signal but increases storage; default 1/100 minimizes cost while preserving regression sensitivity.
We will not bloat existing span model: microhistograms are exported out-of-band to a telemetry topic and only a short span tag with envelope_id is left on traces.
Plan to reuse existing kernel fingerprinting logic (ENG-33321 style) but add a short 8-byte exec_context id to keep telemetry join keys compact.
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize proto and sampling policy; land runtime-only feature flag guard
Week 2: implement emitter in runtime and test in dev clusters with sampling=1/100
Week 3: build ingestion/aggregation and connect to dev Grafana panels
Week 4: canary on dedicated pool (small customer) with traffic ramp; validate overhead and signal fidelity
Week 5: full rollout with default sampling and optional per-customer tuning
risk_mitigation: Kill-switch in config to turn off emission globally
Backpressure: ingestion will drop microhistogram uploads and signal via metric when queue filling
Cost cap: retention defaults to 7 days and can be increased per-customer via billing/console
Data quality: unit tests for sketch merge/deserialize and integration tests with synthetic heavy-tail workloads
